Wrote `spec.md` + `acceptance.md` (overwrote stale task-#95 artifacts that were sitting in the worktree root).

**Root cause found:** `server/bridge.js:149` — `ws.on("close", () => p.kill())`. `TermDrawer`'s effect cleanup closes the socket on unmount, so every tab switch kills the shell. Client-side bug, server-side fix.

**Key spec decision:** intent said *"if possible restore in UI, otherwise pop out native terminal (kitty)"*. It is possible — the PTY already lives in the long-lived bridge process, only the close→kill wiring binds it to a browser tab. So: in-app restoration, native popout dropped. Keeps existing font/ligature settings, cwd header, worktree resolution.

**Shape:** `SESSIONS` map in bridge.js keyed by resolved cwd (already distinguishes repo root vs. each task worktree). Detach clears the socket, leaves the PTY. 256 KB rolling output buffer replayed on reattach. ✕ sends a new `{t:"kill"}` frame so explicit close still kills.

Two things I added that weren't in the intent, both load-bearing:
- **30-min idle reaping of detached sessions** — without it, not killing on detach leaks one shell per terminal ever opened, for the bridge's lifetime. That's a defect the fix would introduce, not a nice-to-have.
- **Explicit kill frame** — otherwise removing the kill leaves no way to end a shell at all.

Scoped out and stated: surviving a dev-server restart, any "running terminals" UI, two panes sharing one session.

One honest limit in the spec: replay is scrollback bytes, not terminal-state emulation. A full-screen TUI (vim, htop) repaints on its next frame or the reattach resize rather than restoring pixel-exact.
